subject: Salem Street Neighborhood Corridor Rezoning Process
overview: The Council addressed significant public concern regarding the Salem Street rezoning process and discussed traffic safety measures following a recent pedestrian fatality. Members also scheduled a special committee meeting for disabled recreation programs and celebrated Black History Month.

items.title: Black History Month Resolution
items.summary: The Council adopted a resolution celebrating Black History Month and reflecting on Medford’s historical figures like Belinda Sutton and the West Medford Community Center.

items.title: Remembrance of Dan Dill and Traffic Safety
items.summary: Approved a memorial resolution for Professor Dan Dill, a pedestrian killed by a vehicle on Mystic Valley Parkway, and referred requests for DCR infrastructure safety improvements to the Committee of the Whole.

items.title: Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved reports from the Planning and Permitting, Resident Services, Governance, and Public Health committees regarding residential zoning, open data, charter review, and reproductive healthcare.

items.title: Salem Street Zoning Public Hearing
items.summary: Opened and continued a public hearing on proposed amendments to the Salem Street neighborhood corridor district to March 11, 2025.

items.title: Business Licenses
items.summary: Tabled a license for Kelly’s Roast Beef due to petitioner absence and approved a license transfer for King Boba Tea.

items.title: Recreation Programs for Disabled Community
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Committee on Education and Culture to discuss department needs and pilot programs for disabled youth and adults on February 25.

items.title: Salem Street Rezoning Communication Process
items.summary: The Council discussed resident frustration regarding the pace and clarity of the Salem Street rezoning project, though a motion to delay the process failed to receive a second.
